sections.heading: What is Markdown and Why Convert to HTML?
sections.content:
Markdown is a lightweight markup language created by John Gruber in 2004. It uses plain text formatting syntax that's easy to read and write, then converts to HTML for web display.

Developers love Markdown because:

- It's human-readable even in raw form
- Works in any text editor
- Supported by GitHub, GitLab, and most documentation platforms
- Faster to write than raw HTML

But web browsers don't understand Markdown directly. To display it on websites, you need to convert it to HTML first. This guide covers all the ways to do that — from free online converters to API integrations.

sections.heading: Markdown to HTML: Common Issues and Fixes
sections.content:
Even simple conversions can hit snags. Here are the most common problems and how to solve them:

**Code blocks not formatting**
Make sure you're using triple backticks (```) and specifying the language: ```javascript not just ```

**Links not rendering**
Markdown links use this syntax: [text](url) — no spaces between ] and (

**Line breaks ignored**
Markdown requires two spaces at end of line or a blank line for new paragraphs. Single line breaks are collapsed.

**Tables not displaying**
Use proper syntax with | and - separators. Not all converters support tables — check your tool's capabilities.

**HTML entities escaped**
If you see < instead of <, your converter is escaping HTML. Look for an option to allow raw HTML.
